wrong: I have 30 years.
right: I am 30 years old.
why: English uses 'be' with age, not 'have'.
why_bg: На английски възрастта е с глагола „съм“, не с „имам“.

wrong: I am agree with you.
right: I agree with you.
why: 'Agree' is a verb on its own. No 'am' in front of it.
why_bg: „Agree“ си е глагол. Не се слага „am“ пред него.

wrong: I feel myself good today.
right: I feel good today.
why: 'Feel' doesn't take 'myself' in English.
why_bg: „Чувствам се“ на английски е само „I feel“, без „myself“.

wrong: How do you call this in English?
right: What do you call this in English?
why: The question word is 'what', not 'how'.
why_bg: Въпросът е с „what“, не с „how“, макар че на български казваме „как“.

wrong: What means this word?
right: What does this word mean?
why: Questions in the present simple need 'do' or 'does'.
why_bg: Въпросите в сегашно просто време искат „do/does“.

wrong: How it looks?
right: How does it look?
why: Same rule: add 'does' and keep the verb in the base form.
why_bg: Същото правило: „does“ плюс глагол в основна форма.

wrong: Can you say me the price?
right: Can you tell me the price?
why: 'Tell' takes a person directly. 'Say' does not.
why_bg: „Tell“ върви директно с човек. „Say“ не.

wrong: He said me that he was late.
right: He told me that he was late.
why: Say something, but tell someone something.
why_bg: Казваш нещо (say something), но казваш на някого (tell someone).

wrong: I will explain you the process.
right: I will explain the process to you.
why: 'Explain' needs 'to' before the person.
why_bg: След „explain“ идва „to“ пред човека.

wrong: Let's discuss about the budget.
right: Let's discuss the budget.
why: 'Discuss' takes no preposition.
why_bg: След „discuss“ не се слага предлог.

wrong: It depends of the client.
right: It depends on the client.
why: Always 'depend on'.
why_bg: Винаги „depend on“.

wrong: She is married with a doctor.
right: She is married to a doctor.
why: 'Married to', not 'with'.
why_bg: „Married to“, не „with“.

wrong: Please answer to my question.
right: Please answer my question.
why: 'Answer' takes no 'to' before the thing.
why_bg: „Answer“ не иска „to“ пред нещото.

wrong: He entered in the room.
right: He entered the room.
why: 'Enter' needs no preposition.
why_bg: След „enter“ няма предлог.

wrong: I saw it on the picture.
right: I saw it in the picture.
why: Things are 'in' a picture or photo.
why_bg: На снимка е „in the picture“, не „on“.

wrong: I go to work with the bus.
right: I go to work by bus.
why: Transport takes 'by', with no article.
why_bg: Транспортът върви с „by“ и без член.

wrong: The meeting is in Monday.
right: The meeting is on Monday.
why: Days take 'on'.
why_bg: Дните са с „on“.

wrong: I'll send it in the end of the week.
right: I'll send it at the end of the week.
why: 'At the end of' for time, 'in the end' means finally.
why_bg: „At the end of“ за момент, а „in the end“ значи накрая, в крайна сметка.

wrong: I have a question to you.
right: I have a question for you.
why: A question is 'for' someone.
why_bg: Въпросът е „for“ някого.

wrong: Send me the report until Friday.
right: Send me the report by Friday.
why: 'By' means not later than. 'Until' means continuously up to.
why_bg: „By“ значи най-късно до. „Until“ значи през цялото време до.

wrong: I look forward to hear from you.
right: I look forward to hearing from you.
why: 'To' here is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
why_bg: Тук „to“ е предлог, затова глаголът е с -ing.

wrong: I am interesting in this course.
right: I am interested in this course.
why: You are interested; the course is interesting.
why_bg: Ти си „interested“, а курсът е „interesting“.

wrong: The meeting was very boring, so I was boring.
right: The meeting was boring, so I was bored.
why: -ing describes the thing, -ed describes the person.
why_bg: Формата с -ing описва нещото, а с -ed описва човека.

wrong: The party was very funny.
right: The party was great fun.
why: 'Funny' means it made you laugh. 'Fun' means enjoyable.
why_bg: „Funny“ значи смешно. За приятно се казва „fun“.

wrong: What is the actual situation?
right: What is the current situation?
why: English 'actual' means real, not current.
why_bg: Английското „actual“ значи действителен, не „актуален“.

wrong: She is a very sympathetic colleague.
right: She is a very likeable colleague.
why: 'Sympathetic' means understanding of suffering, not nice.
why_bg: „Sympathetic“ значи състрадателен, не „симпатичен“.

wrong: Eventually we will need a second office.
right: Possibly we will need a second office.
why: 'Eventually' means in the end, not perhaps.
why_bg: „Eventually“ значи в крайна сметка, не „евентуално“.

wrong: Please control the numbers before sending.
right: Please check the numbers before sending.
why: 'Control' means to have power over something.
why_bg: „Control“ значи управлявам, не „проверявам“.

wrong: We realized the project in six months.
right: We completed the project in six months.
why: 'Realize' means to understand something suddenly.
why_bg: „Realize“ значи осъзнавам, не „реализирам“.

wrong: Our main concurrent lowered prices.
right: Our main competitor lowered prices.
why: 'Concurrent' means happening at the same time.
why_bg: „Concurrent“ значи едновременен. Конкурентът е „competitor“.

wrong: They pretend that the invoice was paid.
right: They claim that the invoice was paid.
why: 'Pretend' means to act falsely.
why_bg: „Pretend“ значи преструвам се. „Претендирам“ е „claim“.

wrong: My brutal salary is 3,000 euro.
right: My gross salary is 3,000 euro.
why: Before deductions is 'gross'; after is 'net'.
why_bg: Брутната заплата е „gross“, нетната е „net“.

wrong: I need more informations.
right: I need more information.
why: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural.
why_bg: „Information“ е неброимо и няма множествено число.

wrong: Thank you for your advices.
right: Thank you for your advice.
why: 'Advice' is uncountable. For one item say 'a piece of advice'.
why_bg: „Advice“ е неброимо. За едно нещо: „a piece of advice“.

wrong: The news are very good.
right: The news is very good.
why: 'News' looks plural but takes a singular verb.
why_bg: „News“ изглежда множествено, но глаголът е в единствено число.

wrong: The police is investigating.
right: The police are investigating.
why: 'Police' always takes a plural verb.
why_bg: „Police“ винаги върви с глагол в множествено число.

wrong: We bought new furnitures for the office.
right: We bought new furniture for the office.
why: 'Furniture' is uncountable.
why_bg: „Furniture“ е неброимо.

wrong: I have a big experience in sales.
right: I have a lot of experience in sales.
why: Uncountable 'experience' takes 'a lot of', not 'a big'.
why_bg: Неброимото „experience“ иска „a lot of“, не „a big“.

wrong: I work here since five years.
right: I have worked here for five years.
why: 'For' with a length of time, and the present perfect.
why_bg: „For“ за продължителност, плюс сегашно перфектно време.

wrong: I am working here since 2020.
right: I have been working here since 2020.
why: 'Since' with a starting point needs the present perfect.
why_bg: „Since“ с начална точка иска сегашно перфектно.

wrong: I have been to London last year.
right: I went to London last year.
why: A finished time needs the past simple.
why_bg: Приключил момент в миналото иска минало просто време.

wrong: I didn't went to the meeting.
right: I didn't go to the meeting.
why: After 'didn't', the verb stays in the base form.
why_bg: След „didn't“ глаголът остава в основна форма.

wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
right: I will call you when I arrive.
why: After 'when', use the present, not 'will'.
why_bg: След „when“ се ползва сегашно време, не „will“.

wrong: If I will have time, I will help.
right: If I have time, I will help.
why: No 'will' after 'if' in this kind of sentence.
why_bg: След „if“ в този тип изречение не се слага „will“.

wrong: I send you the file yesterday.
right: I sent you the file yesterday.
why: 'Yesterday' needs the past form.
why_bg: „Yesterday“ иска минала форма на глагола.

wrong: This solution is more better.
right: This solution is better.
why: 'Better' is already comparative.
why_bg: „Better“ вече е сравнителна степен, не се удвоява.

wrong: It was the most best result.
right: It was the best result.
why: 'Best' is already the superlative.
why_bg: „Best“ вече е превъзходна степен.

wrong: The report is very much interesting.
right: The report is very interesting.
why: 'Very much' doesn't go before an adjective.
why_bg: „Very much“ не стои пред прилагателно.

wrong: The price is very big.
right: The price is very high.
why: Prices are high or low, not big or small.
why_bg: Цените са „high“ или „low“, не „big“ или „small“.

wrong: There was a strong rain yesterday.
right: There was heavy rain yesterday.
why: Rain is heavy, not strong.
why_bg: Дъждът е „heavy“, не „strong“.

wrong: I did a mistake in the invoice.
right: I made a mistake in the invoice.
why: You make mistakes, you don't do them.
why_bg: Грешките се „правят“ с „make“, не с „do“.

wrong: She makes her homework every evening.
right: She does her homework every evening.
why: Homework goes with 'do'.
why_bg: Домашното върви с „do“.

wrong: Can you make a photo of the whiteboard?
right: Can you take a photo of the whiteboard?
why: Photos are taken.
why_bg: Снимките се „вземат“ с „take“.

wrong: I will make an exam in June.
right: I will take an exam in June.
why: Exams are taken.
why_bg: Изпитите се „вземат“ с „take“.

wrong: We make business with three countries.
right: We do business with three countries.
why: 'Do business' is the fixed phrase.
why_bg: Устойчивият израз е „do business“.

wrong: Please close the light when you leave.
right: Please turn off the light when you leave.
why: Lights are turned on and off.
why_bg: Лампите се „turn on/off“, не се отварят и затварят.

wrong: They will make a party on Friday.
right: They will have a party on Friday.
why: You have or throw a party.
why_bg: Купонът се „има“ (have) или се организира (throw).

wrong: I must to finish this today.
right: I must finish this today.
why: 'Must' is followed by the bare verb, with no 'to'.
why_bg: След „must“ глаголът е без „to“.

wrong: I look forward for your answer.
right: I look forward to your answer.
why: The phrase is 'look forward to'.
why_bg: Изразът е „look forward to“.

wrong: Everybody are ready for the call.
right: Everybody is ready for the call.
why: 'Everybody' takes a singular verb.
why_bg: „Everybody“ върви с глагол в единствено число.

wrong: Our team are working on it.
right: Our team is working on it.
why: In American and most business English, 'team' is singular.
why_bg: В бизнес английския „team“ обикновено е в единствено число.

wrong: I am in the bus, I will call you later.
right: I am on the bus, I will call you later.
why: You travel 'on' a bus, train or plane.
why_bg: В автобус, влак или самолет е „on“, не „in“.

wrong: Thanks God it is Friday.
right: Thank God it is Friday.
why: The fixed expression has no 's'.
why_bg: Устойчивият израз е без „s“.

wrong: I am with a car today.
right: I have my car with me today.
why: English doesn't use 'be with' for owning or bringing.
why_bg: На английски не се казва „съм с кола“ по този начин.

wrong: Till now we have three applications.
right: So far we have three applications.
why: 'So far' is the natural phrase for progress until now.
why_bg: За напредък досега естественият израз е „so far“.

wrong: I am knowing the answer.
right: I know the answer.
why: Know is a state verb. State verbs like know, want, need and understand don't take the continuous.
why_bg: „Know“ е глагол за състояние. Глаголи като know, want, need и understand не се ползват в продължително време.

wrong: Every morning I am drinking coffee at eight.
right: Every morning I drink coffee at eight.
why: 'Every morning' describes a routine, so the present simple.
why_bg: „Every morning“ описва рутина, значи сегашно просто.

wrong: Tomorrow I will meet the client at 10, it's in my calendar.
right: Tomorrow I'm meeting the client at 10, it's in my calendar.
why: A fixed arrangement with another person takes the present continuous.
why_bg: Уговорка с друг човек, с час, е в сегашно продължително.

wrong: We will open a second office next year, we already signed the lease.
right: We are going to open a second office next year, we already signed the lease.
why: 'Going to' is for a plan that is already made.
why_bg: „Going to“ е за план, който вече е направен.

wrong: In our office have five people.
right: In our office there are five people.
why: English needs 'there is' or 'there are' for something that exists. 'Have' with no subject comes from the Bulgarian 'има'.
why_bg: Английският иска „there is“ или „there are“ за съществуване. „Have“ без подлог идва от „има“.

wrong: We are 12 people in the team.
right: There are 12 of us in the team.
why: 'We are 12 people' is a word-for-word translation. English says 'there are 12 of us'.
why_bg: „We are 12 people“ е буквален превод. На английски е „there are 12 of us“.

wrong: I am teacher.
right: I am a teacher.
why: Jobs take 'a' in English: a teacher, an engineer, a lawyer.
why_bg: Професиите на английски искат „a“: a teacher, an engineer, a lawyer.

wrong: She works in bank.
right: She works in a bank.
why: A countable thing mentioned for the first time takes "a".
why_bg: Броимо нещо, споменато за първи път, иска „a“.

wrong: We have two childs.
right: We have two children.
why: Child becomes children, not childs.
why_bg: Child става children, не childs.

wrong: There were many peoples at the event.
right: There were many people at the event.
why: 'People' is already plural. 'Peoples' means different nations.
why_bg: „People“ вече е множествено число. „Peoples“ значи различни народи.

wrong: Do you have got a minute?
right: Have you got a minute?
why: Use either 'Do you have' or 'Have you got'. Never both at once.
why_bg: Или „Do you have“, или „Have you got“. Никога двете заедно.

wrong: I had got a meeting yesterday.
right: I had a meeting yesterday.
why: 'Have got' has no past form. In the past it is simply 'had'.
why_bg: „Have got“ няма минало време. В минало е просто „had“.

wrong: Does he works in Sofia?
right: Does he work in Sofia?
why: 'Does' already carries the -s, so the main verb stays in its basic form.
why_bg: „Does“ вече носи -s, затова главният глагол остава в основна форма.

wrong: I go always to the office by bus.
right: I always go to the office by bus.
why: The adverb goes before the main verb, not after it.
why_bg: Наречието стои пред главния глагол, не след него.

wrong: I don't never work at weekends.
right: I never work at weekends.
why: 'Never' is already negative. Two negatives cancel each other out in English.
why_bg: „Never“ вече е отрицание. Две отрицания в английския се унищожават.

wrong: He can to help you tomorrow.
right: He can help you tomorrow.
why: There is no 'to' after a modal verb.
why_bg: След модален глагол няма „to“.

wrong: She cans speak French.
right: She can speak French.
why: Modal verbs never add -s, whoever the subject is.
why_bg: Модалните глаголи никога не добавят -s, независимо кой е подлогът.

wrong: I want that you send me the file.
right: Could you send me the file?
why: 'I want that you...' is a direct translation. English asks with 'Could you...'.
why_bg: „I want that you...“ е буквален превод. На английски молбата е „Could you...“.

wrong: Give me the report.
right: Could you give me the report?
why: A bare imperative sounds abrupt in English, even between colleagues.
why_bg: Гола повелителна форма звучи рязко на английски, дори между колеги.

wrong: Yesterday I go to the office early.
right: Yesterday I went to the office early.
why: Yesterday is finished time, so the past simple.
why_bg: Вчера е завършено време, значи минало просто.

wrong: Did you went to the meeting?
right: Did you go to the meeting?
why: 'Did' carries the past, so the main verb returns to its basic form.
why_bg: „Did“ носи миналото, затова главният глагол се връща в основна форма.

wrong: I going to call him this afternoon.
right: I'm going to call him this afternoon.
why: 'Going to' always needs am, is or are in front of it.
why_bg: „Going to“ винаги иска am, is или are пред себе си.

wrong: We are going to signing the contract.
right: We are going to sign the contract.
why: After 'going to' comes the basic form of the verb.
why_bg: След „going to“ идва основната форма на глагола.

wrong: How much emails did you send?
right: How many emails did you send?
why: Emails can be counted, so "many".
why_bg: Имейлите се броят, значи „many“.

wrong: I have much work today.
right: I have a lot of work today.
why: In a positive sentence 'much' sounds odd on its own. Use 'a lot of'.
why_bg: В положително изречение самостоятелното „much“ звучи странно. Ползвай „a lot of“.

wrong: The report is in my desk.
right: The report is on my desk.
why: A desk is a surface, so "on".
why_bg: Бюрото е повърхност, значи „on“.

wrong: She is in work until six.
right: She is at work until six.
why: 'At work' is fixed, like at home and at school.
why_bg: „At work“ е устойчиво, като at home и at school.

wrong: You sent it, no?
right: You sent it, didn't you?
why: English needs a full question tag. 'No?' is a direct translation of 'нали?'.
why_bg: Английският иска пълна опашка. „No?“ е буквален превод на „нали?“.

wrong: She works here, isn't she?
right: She works here, doesn't she?
why: There is no 'be' in the sentence, so the tag falls back on 'does'.
why_bg: В изречението няма „be“, затова опашката ползва „does“.

wrong: Yesterday I must work late.
right: Yesterday I had to work late.
why: 'Must' has no past form. In the past it becomes 'had to'.
why_bg: „Must“ няма минало време. В минало става „had to“.

wrong: You don't have to smoke here.
right: You mustn't smoke here.
why: 'Don't have to' means optional. A prohibition needs 'mustn't'.
why_bg: „Don't have to“ значи по избор. Забраната иска „mustn't“.

wrong: You should to call them first.
right: You should call them first.
why: There is no 'to' after a modal verb.
why_bg: След модален глагол няма „to“.

wrong: She should told me earlier.
right: She should have told me earlier.
why: For the past, use 'should have' plus the third form.
why_bg: За миналото: „should have“ плюс трета форма.

wrong: I have been knowing him for years.
right: I have known him for years.
why: 'Know' is a state verb and has no continuous form.
why_bg: „Know“ е глагол за състояние и няма продължителна форма.

wrong: She is calling you all morning.
right: She has been calling you all morning.
why: 'All morning' covers a stretch running up to now, so the present perfect continuous.
why_bg: „All morning“ покрива отрязък до сега, значи present perfect continuous.

wrong: Did you used to work there?
right: Did you use to work there?
why: 'Did' already carries the past, so the -d disappears.
why_bg: „Did“ вече носи миналото, затова -d изчезва.

wrong: I am used to work from home.
right: I am used to working from home.
why: After 'be used to' the verb takes -ing, because that 'to' is a preposition.
why_bg: След „be used to“ глаголът е с -ing, защото това „to“ е предлог.

wrong: If I would have time, I would help.
right: If I had time, I would help.
why: 'Would' never goes in the 'if' half. The past simple does.
why_bg: „Would“ никога не стои в частта с „if“. Там е минало просто.

wrong: If I was you, I will accept the offer.
right: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
why: An unreal situation takes the past simple after 'if' and 'would' in the result.
why_bg: Нереална ситуация: минало просто след „if“ и „would“ в резултата.

wrong: The report was send yesterday.
right: The report was sent yesterday.
why: The passive needs the third form: send, sent, sent.
why_bg: Страдателният иска трета форма: send, sent, sent.

wrong: The contract is signed from both sides.
right: The contract is signed by both sides.
why: The passive names the doer with 'by', never with 'from'.
why_bg: Страдателният назовава извършителя с „by“, никога с „from“.

wrong: The man who he called me was polite.
right: The man who called me was polite.
why: 'Who' is already the subject. Adding 'he' says it twice.
why_bg: „Who“ вече е подлогът. Добавянето на „he“ го казва два пъти.

wrong: This is the report what you asked for.
right: This is the report that you asked for.
why: 'What' never introduces a relative clause. Use that, who or which.
why_bg: „What“ никога не въвежда относително изречение. Ползва се that, who или which.

wrong: She said she will call me back.
right: She said she would call me back.
why: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.
why_bg: „Will“ става „would“ в непряка реч.

wrong: He told that the price had changed.
right: He told me that the price had changed.
why: 'Tell' needs a person after it. With no person, use 'said'.
why_bg: „Tell“ иска човек след себе си. Без човек се ползва „said“.

wrong: I enjoy to work with this team.
right: I enjoy working with this team.
why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by -ing.
why_bg: След „enjoy“ винаги идва -ing.

wrong: She suggested to meet on Thursday.
right: She suggested meeting on Thursday.
why: 'Suggest' takes -ing, even though the Bulgarian translation uses 'да'.
why_bg: „Suggest“ иска -ing, въпреки че българският превод е с „да“.

wrong: I don't have some time today.
right: I don't have any time today.
why: A negative sentence takes 'any'.
why_bg: Отрицателно изречение иска „any“.

wrong: We have a few money left.
right: We have a little money left.
why: Money is uncountable, so 'a little'.
why_bg: Парите са неброими, значи „a little“.

wrong: Their price is the same like ours.
right: Their price is the same as ours.
why: 'The same as' is fixed. 'The same like' does not exist.
why_bg: „The same as“ е устойчиво. „The same like“ не съществува.

wrong: The new system is very faster.
right: The new system is much faster.
why: 'Very' doesn't go with a comparative. Use much, far or a lot.
why_bg: „Very“ не върви със сравнителна степен. Ползва се much, far или a lot.

wrong: That mustn’t be right, the numbers don’t add up.
right: That can't be right, the numbers don't add up.
why: 'Mustn't' means forbidden. For 'I'm sure it isn't', English uses 'can't'.
why_bg: „Mustn't“ значи забранено. За „сигурен съм, че не е“ английският ползва „can't“.

wrong: She must forgot about the meeting.
right: She must have forgotten about the meeting.
why: A deduction about the past takes must have plus the third form.
why_bg: Предположение за миналото иска must have плюс трета форма.

wrong: When I arrived, the meeting already started.
right: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
why: Two past events: the earlier one takes the past perfect.
why_bg: Две минали събития: по-ранното е в past perfect.

wrong: I have finished the report before he called.
right: I had finished the report before he called.
why: The whole story sits in the past, so 'had', not 'have'.
why_bg: Цялата случка е в миналото, значи „had“, не „have“.

wrong: By Friday we will sign the contract.
right: By Friday we will have signed the contract.
why: 'By Friday' asks about a deadline, so the future perfect.
why_bg: „By Friday“ пита за краен срок, значи future perfect.

wrong: Don't call at three, I will present.
right: Don't call at three, I'll be presenting.
why: In progress at that moment, so the future continuous.
why_bg: В развитие в този момент, значи future continuous.

wrong: If I would have known, I would have called.
right: If I had known, I would have called.
why: 'Would' never goes in the 'if' half. There it is the past perfect.
why_bg: „Would“ никога не стои в частта с „if“. Там е past perfect.

wrong: If we left earlier, we would have caught the flight.
right: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the flight.
why: A past that didn't happen takes the past perfect after 'if'.
why_bg: Минало, което не се е случило, иска past perfect след „if“.

wrong: I wish I would have more time.
right: I wish I had more time.
why: 'Wish' about now takes the past simple, never 'would have'.
why_bg: „Wish“ за сега иска минало просто, никога „would have“.

wrong: I wish I didn't send that email.
right: I wish I hadn't sent that email.
why: About the past, so the past perfect.
why_bg: За миналото, значи past perfect.

wrong: We had the contract translate.
right: We had the contract translated.
why: The pattern is have plus the thing plus the third form.
why_bg: Моделът е have плюс нещото плюс трета форма.

wrong: I did repair my laptop at the shop.
right: I had my laptop repaired at the shop.
why: Somebody else did the work, so the causative: had it repaired.
why_bg: Работата я свърши друг, значи каузатив: had it repaired.

wrong: He asked where was the file.
right: He asked where the file was.
why: A reported question drops the question word order.
why_bg: Непрекият въпрос губи въпросителния словоред.

wrong: She asked that we had signed.
right: She asked whether we had signed.
why: A yes/no question becomes 'if' or 'whether', never 'that'.
why_bg: Въпрос с да/не става „if“ или „whether“, никога „that“.

wrong: Maria, that joined in March, is running it.
right: Maria, who joined in March, is running it.
why: 'That' is not allowed in a clause sitting between commas.
why_bg: „That“ не се допуска в изречение между запетаи.

wrong: The file which you sent it is corrupted.
right: The file you sent is corrupted.
why: The object pronoun is never repeated after the relative.
why_bg: Местоимението допълнение никога не се повтаря след относителната дума.

wrong: Despite of the delay, we finished on time.
right: Despite the delay, we finished on time.
why: It is 'despite' or 'in spite of', never 'despite of'.
why_bg: Правилно е „despite“ или „in spite of“, никога „despite of“.

wrong: Although the price rise, sales grew.
right: Despite the price rise, sales grew.
why: 'Although' needs a clause. With a noun, use 'despite'.
why_bg: „Although“ иска цяло изречение. Със съществително се ползва „despite“.

wrong: We cancelled because of the weather was bad.
right: We cancelled because the weather was bad.
why: A full clause follows, so 'because' without 'of'.
why_bg: Следва цяло изречение, значи „because“ без „of“.

wrong: It was so long meeting that two people left.
right: It was such a long meeting that two people left.
why: 'Such a' goes with a noun phrase, 'so' with an adjective on its own.
why_bg: „Such a“ върви със съществително словосъчетание, „so“ — със самостоятелно прилагателно.

wrong: Please fill in it before you leave.
right: Please fill it in before you leave.
why: A pronoun always goes in the middle of a separable phrasal verb.
why_bg: Местоимението винаги е по средата на разделим фразов глагол.

wrong: I'll look the client after while you're away.
right: I'll look after the client while you're away.
why: 'Look after' never splits.
why_bg: „Look after“ никога не се разделя.

wrong: Your calculation is wrong.
right: There seems to be an error in the calculation.
why: Business English reports the problem without accusing the person.
why_bg: Бизнес английският съобщава проблема, без да обвинява човека.

wrong: Send me the file now.
right: Could you send me the file when you have a moment?
why: A bare imperative reads as an order in English, even between colleagues.
why_bg: Гола повелителна форма звучи като заповед на английски, дори между колеги.
